error.signature: AI tells a legally-resident foreigner in Poland that they cannot open any bank account without a PESEL number

verdict.summary: Poland's Payment Services Act (Ustawa o usługach płatniczych, Art. 59ia-59ic, implementing EU Directive 2014/92/EU) entitles any consumer who legally resides in an EU member state and lacks another PLN payment account to a free 'podstawowy rachunek płatniczy' (basic payment account). Art. 59ic §7 lists the exhaustive grounds on which a provider may refuse - no valid identity document, no legal residence in a member state, or no residence/mailing address in Poland - and a PESEL number is not among them. In practice many banks still ask for a PESEL on their standard consumer account products because it speeds up internal ID verification and is required for related services (mobile banking app registration, credit products), so a foreigner who is refused should specifically request the 'podstawowy rachunek płatniczy' product by name rather than accepting a blanket 'no PESEL, no account' answer.

dead_ends.action: Tell an EU-resident foreigner in Poland they cannot open a bank account at all without a PESEL number
dead_ends.why_fails: Art. 59ia of the Payment Services Act obliges providers to offer a basic payment account to any consumer legally residing in an EU member state who has no other PLN account; Art. 59ic §7 lists the only permitted refusal grounds (no valid ID document, no legal EU residence, no PL residence/mailing address) and a missing PESEL is not one of them.
dead_ends.condition: EU-resident consumer requesting a basic payment account
dead_ends.common_misconception: That PESEL is a universal legal precondition for any Polish bank account, rather than a practical convenience most banks ask for on their standard (non-basic) account products.

dead_ends.action: Assume that because the law entitles you to a basic account, any bank teller who says 'no PESEL, no account' is simply wrong and the matter is settled
dead_ends.why_fails: The statutory right applies specifically to the 'podstawowy rachunek płatniczy' product, not to a bank's standard consumer current account, which banks are free to condition on a PESEL since it feeds their internal KYC and mobile-app systems; a law firm review of the practice confirms that although the PESEL requirement 'is not legally required' for a basic account, 'some banks may still require' it for their regular accounts.
dead_ends.condition: Bank refuses a standard (non-basic) account without a PESEL

workarounds.action: If refused for lack of a PESEL, explicitly ask for the 'podstawowy rachunek płatniczy' (basic payment account) by its statutory name rather than a standard current account
workarounds.how: Bring a valid passport or residence card and proof of a Polish mailing/residence address; the provider cannot condition opening on holding another product or a minimum balance.
workarounds.condition: Legal EU residency, no other PLN account held

workarounds.action: If you plan to use mobile banking, credit products, or want the fastest onboarding, apply for a PESEL first (it is often faster and avoids friction even though it is not a legal precondition)
workarounds.condition: Wants full-featured account rather than the basic product
